rich_summary: This section depicts the climactic struggle between Lakshmana and Indrajit during the war in Lanka. After Angada destroys Indrajit’s chariot with a hurled tree, the Rakshasa prince turns invisible and devastates the battlefield with divine arrows, binding Rama and Lakshmana in a deadly net. The monkey army gathers in despair until Vibhishana revives the brothers and provides sacred water from Kuvera that allows them to see invisible foes. When Indrajit returns to battle before completing his sacrificial rites, Lakshmana confronts him. In a decisive duel, Lakshmana severs Indrajit’s arms and finally his head with three blazing arrows. The victory breaks Ravana’s greatest military advantage, but the grief-stricken demon king, maddened by loss, nearly turns his fury upon the captive Sita.

highlight_spans.why: Opening escalation of the battle showing Indrajit unleashing javelins and Lakshmana calmly destroying them, establishing the duel’s intensity.
Angada’s dramatic act of hurling a massive tree that destroys Indrajit’s chariot, forcing the Rakshasa prince to vanish using illusion.
Rama and Lakshmana fall under Indrajit’s invisible assault, described with the striking image of the Sun and Moon fallen from the sky.
The pivotal moment where Lakshmana kills Indrajit with three arrows—severing both arms and then the head—ending Ravana’s most formidable champion.
Ravana’s grief upon seeing the empty chariot and learning of his son’s death, leading to his desperate impulse to kill Sita.

top_scenes.scene_text: Angada, roaring in fury, smashes Indrajit’s chariot by hurling a massive tree while warriors clash amid flying arrows.
Rama and Lakshmana lie on the battlefield bound in a glowing net of arrows while the monkey army gathers anxiously around them.
Lakshmana releases three blazing arrows that sever Indrajit’s arms and head as the Rakshasa prince collapses on the battlefield.
